meaning: A small label at the top of a web browser. Each one holds a different page, so you can switch between them.
clues: They line up along the top edge, like the tabs on file folders.
Click one to see a different web page without losing the others.
Each one shows a tiny picture and the name of its page.
Click the little x on one to close just that page.
It has two words. The first is the program you use to visit websites.
assumes: A browser window is a frame that holds web pages
A bookmark is a saved shortcut to a page
Browsing history is a list of pages you visited

decoys.meaning: A separate frame on the screen that holds one or more web pages.
A saved shortcut to a web page you want to find again.
A list of the web pages you have visited before.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: File folders had tabs sticking out of the side. Same idea, except yours can play video!

exchange.text: Tip: too many open tabs can slow things down. Close the ones you are finished with.
